- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.53) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak to avoid overcorrection.
- In low sentiment (≤0.27) periods, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward higher levels.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >5% in 3–5 consecutive days, assume momentum bias — adjust next forecast downward by 2–4% to reflect diminishing momentum.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.80, 0.27, 0.80), model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently underestimates in early days (e.g., 1–5 days) and sentiment is neutral or positive, add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast to capture initial momentum.
